Nikopol Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Nikopol's earliest known Jewish community dates to the 1780s, reaching 322 people by 1847 and growing tenfold to 3,284 (of 17,097 total) by 1897, supported by three synagogues and a private Jewish secondary school by 1910. In 1913, Jews owned three drug stores, all three pharmacy goods warehouses in town, a hotel, and more than 40 shops. Following the August 1941 occupation, a ghetto was established; 130 Jews were murdered on October 3, and 570 more two days later, with additional executions continuing into 1942. Some Jews returned after the war, and the community was formally revived in 1996, numbering around 1,100 by 2005. This cemetery, per the Commission on the Preservation of Jewish Heritage founded in the 19th century, was demolished in the 1960s and overbuilt with a maternity hospital and apartment block; its last known burial took place in the late 1940s or early 1950s.
